q1.question: What is VVTerm?
q1.answer: VVTerm is an SSH terminal app for iOS and macOS. It lets you manage and connect to remote servers with iCloud sync across your Apple devices.

q2.question: How does iCloud sync work?
q2.answer: Server configurations sync via iCloud to all your devices. Passwords and SSH keys are stored in Apple Keychain and can sync via iCloud Keychain when enabled.

q3.question: Which connection methods are supported?
q3.answer: VVTerm supports standard SSH plus Mosh, Tailscale SSH, and Cloudflare Tunnel SSH. Credentials stay secured in Apple Keychain when required.

q4.question: Does VVTerm work on iPad?
q4.answer: Yes. VVTerm works on iPhone, iPad, and Mac, and the iOS version includes a keyboard toolbar with Esc, Tab, Ctrl, and arrow keys.

q5.question: What terminal engine does it use?
q5.answer: VVTerm uses libghostty, the same rendering engine from Ghostty, for fast and accurate terminal emulation.

q6.question: What is included in Free vs Pro?
q6.answer: Free includes 1 workspace, 1 server, and 1 connection tab. Pro unlocks unlimited workspaces, servers, simultaneous connections, and custom environments.

q7.question: Can I use one purchase on multiple devices?
q7.answer: Yes. Your Pro purchase syncs through the App Store. Sign in with the same Apple ID on your devices to unlock Pro everywhere.

q8.question: What is the refund policy?
q8.answer: Refunds are handled by Apple through the App Store. To request one, use Apple's refund flow at reportaproblem.apple.com.

q9.question: What are the system requirements?
q9.answer: iOS 16+ on iPhone and iPad, or macOS 13+ Ventura on Apple Silicon Macs. Intel Macs are not supported.

q10.question: Does VVTerm include remote file browsing?
q10.answer: Yes. VVTerm includes a built-in SFTP Files view for browsing folders, previewing text, image, and video files, uploading and downloading, renaming or moving items, creating folders, and editing POSIX permissions on supported servers.

connect.title: Reach any machine, four ways.
connect.body: Use standard SSH when you want it and Mosh, Tailscale SSH, or Cloudflare Tunnel SSH when you need them — no extra tools to juggle.
connect.caption: Switch transports per server.

tmux.title: Sessions that survive the drop.
tmux.body: VVTerm manages tmux for you, so a long build or migration keeps running when your connection blinks, your phone sleeps, or you switch apps. It auto-installs tmux, ships a tuned config, and reattaches the moment you reconnect.

custom.title: Make it yours.
custom.body: 440 built-in themes, Nerd Fonts, cursor styles, and a keyboard toolbar you build with your own command snippets and shortcuts — synced across devices.

monitor.title: Watch it live.
monitor.body: CPU, memory, network, disk, load, and top processes in real time — right beside your shell, on Linux, macOS, BSD, and Windows hosts.

files.title: An SFTP browser, right beside your shell.
files.body: Browse remote folders, upload and download, create directories, rename, move, and delete — then preview text, images, and video or edit POSIX permissions, all without a second app.
files.modalTitle: Everything you need for remote files.
files.modalBody: A full file manager built into VVTerm — browse, upload, download, rename, move, and delete, create folders, preview text, images, and video, edit supported text files, and adjust POSIX permissions on servers that allow it.
files.card0body: Move through remote folders, then rename, move, delete, and create directories in place.
files.card1body: Upload from your device and download to it — single files or whole folders over SFTP.
files.card2body: Open text, images, and video right in VVTerm without downloading them first.
files.card3body: Make quick edits to supported text files and save them straight back to the server.
files.card4body: Inspect and adjust owner, group, and other permission bits on servers that allow it.
files.card5body: Jump between the terminal and the file browser for the same server without switching apps.
files.outroTitle: No second app. No context switch.
files.outroBody: Most SSH clients send you to a separate SFTP app for file work. VVTerm keeps files and terminal together, so checking a config, fixing a permission, or pulling a log never breaks your flow.

voice.title: Talk to your terminal.
voice.body: Dictate commands on the go with on-device transcription. VVTerm turns speech into shell input using MLX models or Apple Speech — useful when you are away from a keyboard.
